entities.name: Battle of Aquae Sextiae
entities.label: EventWindow
entities.summary:
The Battle of Aquae Sextiae was the climactic 102 bce showdown of the Cimbrian War, a pivotal struggle for control of Western Europe.

This fateful confrontation took place in the Roman province of Gallia, in what is now modern-day southern France, on June 6, 101 bce.

The battle marked a decisive turning point in the Cimbrian War, as the Roman legions under the leadership of Gaius Marius triumphantly defeated the Germanic Cimbri, led by the chieftain Viriathus.

The Roman victory at Aquae Sextiae not only secured Marius's reputation as one of the greatest generals of the Roman Republic but also paved the way for Rome's expansion into Europe, forever altering the course of Western civilization.

As the Roman historian Plutarch aptly noted, 'The Cimbri, being vanquished, were either sold into slavery or driven out of their country, and the Romans, having acquired the sovereignty of the Gallic provinces, were the first to make the Rhine their boundary.'
